name: Collin Brown
title: Workplace Experience Manager
one_liner: 7+ years turning empty shells into offices people are genuinely glad to walk into. Most recently a 13,000 sq ft, 3-floor SF build-out run with no general contractor, plus the vendors, budgets, and everyday details that make a space work for the people in it.
bio: What keeps me in this work is simple: a good workplace changes how people feel and what they're able to do. When a space is easy to use, well stocked, and actually feels good to be in, people have what they need to focus, do their best work, and want to be there. Over 7+ years across San Francisco's tech, nonprofit, and coworking offices, I've learned that comes down to owning the details most people only notice when they're missing: facilities, vendors, budgets, onboarding, and the small touches and events that make a place feel alive. To me the physical space and the culture are the same job: take care of both, and people can do more and be more.
currently: Currently running workplace experience for a security-compliance company's SF headquarters with Cushman & Wakefield, including an HQ relocation

stats.label: Years in Workplace Ops
stats.story: Across tech, nonprofit, and coworking environments in San Francisco, from front desk to ground-up HQ build-out.

stats.label: People Moved, Zero Downtime

skill_descriptions.Workplace Operations: Workplace operations is the core of my practice: owning the systems, spaces, and logistics that keep an office running reliably. I approach it broadly rather than as a narrow function, which means I'm comfortable owning both tactical execution and the strategic setup that makes scale possible.
skill_descriptions.Facilities Management: I've run facilities across multi-floor commercial build-outs, coworking spaces, and corporate offices: daily walkthroughs, building-management liaison work, and the physical environment end-to-end. My focus is operational reliability: making sure the space never becomes a distraction for the people working in it.
skill_descriptions.Vendor & Contractor Management: Vendor and contractor management is where I tend to have the most direct financial and operational impact. I handle the full lifecycle — sourcing, negotiating, onboarding, oversight, and accountability — across everything from local trades to enterprise operators like CBRE, Knotel, and WeWork.
skill_descriptions.Space Planning: Space planning is one of the more creative parts of my work — translating headcount, workflow, and culture into a physical layout. I've applied it at the scale of full multi-floor build-outs and modular event-space remodels, always working to make the space serve the people using it.
skill_descriptions.Budget Management: I treat budget control as a core responsibility, not an afterthought. I've delivered projects $30K under budget, disputed inflated vendor quotes, and found mid-project savings — being deliberate about spend from day one rather than reconciling at the end.
skill_descriptions.Employee Experience: Employee experience shapes how I think about almost everything in a workplace: what does it feel like to work here, and what can operations do to improve that? I've built concession programs, engagement initiatives, and biophilic office environments specifically to make people want to come in and stay engaged.
skill_descriptions.Event Programming: I plan and execute workplace events from All-Hands and off-sites to client events, team-building, and seasonal programming. My focus is events with a clear purpose — building community, signaling care, or reinforcing culture — rather than just filling a calendar.
skill_descriptions.Onboarding & Offboarding: I've owned onboarding and offboarding operations including access control, hardware provisioning, and workspace readiness. The goal is a seamless Day 1 for new hires and a clean, well-documented exit process that protects the organization.
skill_descriptions.AV/IT Systems: I've owned AV and workplace technology across multiple sites — conference-room AV, Zoom-enabled rooms, digital signage, network, and print services. I'm not a dedicated IT specialist, but I'm comfortable owning these systems operationally and partnering with IT on deeper technical work.
skill_descriptions.Building Security & Safety: I partner closely with building security and safety teams on access control, inspections, and emergency response protocols. It's the less visible side of workplace operations — keeping the building's systems and the company's needs aligned and the environment safe.
skill_descriptions.Process Documentation: I build service catalogs, playbooks, and documentation as a natural output of the work. The goal is always the same: reduce dependency on knowledge living in one person's head and make it possible for someone else to run the same process faster next time. At Klaviyo I wrote a working SOP covering onboarding, office moves and setup, vendor and COI, and ticket intake that others followed.
skill_descriptions.Stakeholder Management: Working across departments and leadership levels is constant in this role. I'm comfortable managing up, across, and laterally — aligning executives on a construction timeline, partnering with IT and People Ops, or serving as the concierge point of contact for a 500+ person organization.
